L86: 
L87: Reliable access to open coding models with two usage tiers.
L88: 
L89: OpenCode Go gives you reliable access to popular open coding models, with two monthly plans:
L90: 
L91: Plan  | Price  | Included usage
L92: --- | --- | ---
L93: Go  | $10/month  | Lower-cost access to the models below
L94: Go Plus  | $40/month  | Higher usage limits across the models below
L95: 
L96: Go works like any other provider in OpenCode. You subscribe to OpenCode Go and get your API key. It’s completely optional and you don’t need to use it to use OpenCode.
L97: The service is designed primarily for international users and provides stable global access.
L98: 
L99: * * *
L100: ## cite39†Background L101: 
L102: Open models have gotten really good. They now reach performance close to proprietary models for coding tasks. And because many providers can serve them competitively, they are usually far cheaper.
L103: 
L104: However, getting reliable, low latency access to them can be difficult. Providers vary in quality and availability.
L105: 
L106: Tip
L107: 
L108: We tested a select group of models and providers that work well with OpenCode.
L109: 
L110: To fix this, we did a couple of things:
L111:   1. We tested a select group of open models and talked to their teams about how to best run them.
L112:   2. We then worked with a few providers to make sure these were being served correctly.
L113:   3. Finally, we benchmarked the combination of the model/provider and came up with a list that we feel good recommending.
L114: 
L115: Both Go and Go Plus provide access to these models; choose the plan that fits how much you use them.
L116: 
L117: * * *
L118: ## cite40†How it works L119: 
L120: OpenCode Go works like any other provider in OpenCode.
L121: 
L122:   1. You sign in to cite52†OpenCode Console , subscribe to Go or Go Plus, and copy your API key.
L123:   2. You run the `/connect` command in the TUI, select `OpenCode Go`, and paste your API key.
L124:   3. Run `/models` in the TUI to see the list of models available through Go.
L125: 
L126: Note
L127: 
L128: Only one member per workspace can subscribe to OpenCode Go or Go Plus.
L129: 
L130: The current list of models includes:

L165: * * *
L166: ## cite41†Where can I use it? L167: 
L168: OpenCode Go is designed for cite2†OpenCode and other coding agents that produce similar types of requests. Traffic is monitored for abuse that degrades the experience for other users.
L169: 
L170: Your client should:
L171:   1. Send typical coding agent traffic
L172:   2. Identify itself with its own user agent, such as `my-coding-agent/1.0`, rather than a generic SDK or HTTP-library name.
L173:   3. Send a stable session ID in `x-opencode-session` for each conversation so we can optimize routing and prompt caching.
L174: ### cite42†Validated Clients L175: 
L176: Besides OpenCode, the following clients have been validated to work properly with OpenCode Go. Although we do not guarantee that they will continue to work in the future.
L177: Client  | Session support
L178: --- | ---
L179: Hermes  | Builds containing cite54†PR #101864†github.com send the header on main and auxiliary OpenCode requests. The fix was merged after v0.21.0; that release alone does not include it.
L180: Claude Code  | Go recognizes its native session header. No custom-header wrapper is needed.
L181: Codex  | Go recognizes its native session header. Some versions and proxy setups still omit it; preserve the session header when forwarding requests.
L182: ZCode  | Go recognizes its native session header. Our cite55†request for `x-opencode-session`†github.com remains open, but it is no longer necessary to send that specific header.
L183: Pi  | Current builds send session information for OpenCode. Update older installations.
L184: jcode  | Update to v0.81.6 or later, which includes the cite56†session-header fix†github.com .
L185: Kilo Code CLI  | Builds containing cite57†PR #13752†github.com restore OpenCode session headers. This fix covers the CLI, not the VS Code extension. See cite58†issue #13723†github.com .
L186: ### cite43†Known Problematic Clients L187: 
L188: These clients have missing or incomplete session support in the versions we investigated. The linked reports track fixes and workarounds.
